name: Token Attachment Origin Validation
description: Prevents bearer tokens from being sent to third-party origins by validating all Authorization headers against the allow-list.
message:
[Security Check] Token attachment detected. Verify:
  1. Is this in the authInterceptor (only place Authorization should be set)?
  2. Does the interceptor check allowedOrigins allow-list?
  3. Is HttpClient used (not fetch or XMLHttpRequest)?

Bearing tokens sent to third-party origins = reportable security incident.

name: Open Redirect Prevention
description: Detects potential open redirect vulnerabilities where returnUrl is used without validation.
message:
[Security Check] Return URL detected. Verify:
  1. Is returnUrl validated to start with '/' and not '//'?
  2. Is navigateByUrl used only after validation?
  3. For guards: is the URL created from state.url?

Unvalidated returnUrl = open redirect vulnerability.

name: Token Storage Security
description: Prevents tokens from being stored in localStorage, which is vulnerable to XSS and persists beyond logout.
message:
[Security Error] Token found in localStorage or sessionStorage.
Tokens must be stored in memory only (signal() in services).
Reason: localStorage persists across sessions and is vulnerable to XSS.
SessionStorage expires but is still world-readable.
Use signal() and refresh token for silent refresh instead.

name: Single Interceptor Rule
description: Ensures Authorization headers are set in exactly one place (the interceptor), preventing inconsistent token attachment.
message:
[Security Check] Authorization header set in a service.
All Authorization headers must go through the auth interceptor only.
Reason: Setting headers in multiple places guarantees you'll forget one.

Move this to the authInterceptor in withInterceptors([authInterceptor]).

name: Token in Logs Prevention
description: Detects potential token leakage in console.log, console.error, or error messages.
message:
[Security Check] Token or sensitive data may be logged.
Reason: Logs appear in DevTools, error trackers, and aggregation systems.
Tokens in logs = credentials leaked to third parties.

Remove tokens from all console output, error messages, and logs.
Log error status/message only, never the token or customer data.

name: Route Guard Enforcement
description: Reminds developers to add canActivate guards to all protected routes.
message:
[Security Check] Routes configuration detected.
Verify:
  1. Every route except '/sign-in' has canActivate: [authGuard]
  2. authGuard validates isAuthenticated()
  3. authGuard redirects to '/sign-in' if not authenticated

Without guards, unauthenticated users can reach protected routes.

name: Generated Clients Must Be Committed
description: Ensures generated API clients are committed to git, not gitignored.
message:
[Configuration Error] Generated API clients are gitignored.
Generated clients MUST be committed.

Reason: Cloning the repo should build without Java runtime or network access.
Contract changes should appear as diffs reviewers read.

Remove generated/ from .gitignore. Keep the generator command and version in README.

name: Environment Secrets Protection
description: Ensures .env files are not committed and secrets are properly configured.
message:
[Configuration Check] .env protection in place.
Verify:
  1. .env is in .gitignore
  2. .env.example is committed (template)
  3. Team members copy .env.example to .env and fill in values
  4. No secrets (API keys, tokens, credentials) in .env.example

name: Interceptor Test Coverage
description: Reminds developers to test both attach and do-not-attach cases for the auth interceptor.
message:
[Testing Reminder] Interceptor tests detected.
Verify test coverage:
  1. Test named 'should attach bearer token to own API requests'
  2. Test named 'should NOT attach bearer token to third-party requests'
  3. Both tests using HttpTestingController with appropriate mocks

These two test cases are explicitly assessed in the review.
